chunks: As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from more than one of our companions, he said:

A grave-robbing man was brought to Amīr al-Muʾminīn, so Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام seized him by his hair and struck him against the ground. Then he ordered the people, and they trampled him until he died.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.فَضَرَبَ بِهِ الْأَرْضَ: he struck him against the ground
key_terms.نَبَّاشٍ: a grave robber; one who digs up graves

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām narrate about the punishment of a grave robber by Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith reports an incident in which Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام dealt with a grave robber in an extremely severe manner. It appears in a legal chapter concerning theft, betrayal, snatching, grave-digging, strangulation, and corruption in the land, indicating its relevance to judicial rulings and punishment.
